2609.08765.title: Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent: A Reliability Audit of Cybersecurity LLM Benchmarks
2609.08765.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) benchmarks are often treated as fixed datasets with stable scores, yet their outcomes depend on configurable evaluation pipelines. We audit eight cybersecurity benchmarks across 10 proprietary, open-weight, and cybersecurity-specialized LLMs. By modeling benchmarks as measurement pipelines, we identify 15 systematic failure modes and show that a single pipeline choice can change a model's score by more than 80 percentage points and substantially alter model rankings. At the cross-benchmark level, two semantically similar task pairs rank the same models differently because of incompatible evaluation conventions. Under an evaluation harness that standardizes pipeline choices while preserving task semantics, nine of 10 models shift by at least three ranks on at least one benchmark. These results show that cybersecurity LLM benchmark scores are pipeline-dependent and motivate pipeline-aware auditing as a core requirement for reliable model evaluation.
2609.08765.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）基準通常被視為具有穩定分數的固定數據集，然而它們的結果取決於可配置的評估流程。<lb/>我們對十個專有的、開放權重的以及專注於網絡安全的 LLM 進行了八個網絡安全基準的審核。<lb/>通過將基準建模為測量流程，我們識別出 15 種系統性失效模式，並顯示單一的流程選擇可以使模型的分數變化超過 80 個百分點，並顯著改變模型排名。<lb/>在跨基準層面上，兩對語義相似的任務組合因為不兼容的評估規範而對同一模型的排名不同。<lb/>在一個標準化流程選擇的評估環境下，同時保留任務語義，十個模型中有九個在至少一個基準上至少變動三個排名。<lb/>這些結果顯示網絡安全 LLM 基準分數依賴於流程，並促使流程意識的審核成為可靠模型評估的核心要求。
